title: replace historical Envoy service routing with ECS Service Connect
input: The platform team inventories virtual services, retry policies and TLS dependencies before moving an existing mesh.
action: App Mesh historically distributed routing configuration to Envoy proxies. Proxies intercepted service calls and selected upstream targets; application containers executed the order logic.
output: Deploy equivalent service discovery and routing in ECS Service Connect, then move one caller at a time.
check: Compare allowed upstreams, timeouts, retries and error rates before removing the old proxies.

title: build an internal purchase approval application
input: A procurement owner defines purchase fields, approval roles and the approved business data connection.
action: App Studio helps build an internal application with pages, data entities and automation. Configure its connector to the approved purchasing system and restrict application access to the assigned employees.
output: Purchasing staff submit requests; the approval automation records an authorized manager's decision through the configured connector.
check: Test that requesters cannot approve their own purchases and connector credentials cannot access unrelated records.

title: normalize historical SaaS audit evidence for investigation
input: The security team selects supported SaaS tenants and their audit-log authorization scopes.
action: AppFabric for security collected supported SaaS audit logs and normalized them for downstream security analysis. Connector authorization and delivery destinations determined which tenant events were collected.
output: The investigator correlates normalized user activity with the incident timeline and exports only permitted evidence.
check: Compare source tenant events with delivered records and document connector or collection gaps.

title: adjust application resources under a scaling plan
input: The application owner selects supported scalable resources, utilization targets and minimum capacity.
action: AWS Auto Scaling scaling plans coordinate supported resource scaling policies using configured targets. Scaling changes capacity; it does not evaluate shopping-cart rules or route individual HTTP requests.
output: The application continues serving requests while supported compute capacity is adjusted under the selected policies.
check: Load-test scale-out, cooldown and scale-in while confirming required minimum capacity remains available.

title: translate a partner purchase order into application JSON
input: A supplier delivers an agreed EDI purchase-order document to the restricted input location.
action: B2B Data Interchange uses the configured partnership, trading-capability and transformer to convert supported EDI transactions to the selected structured format. Mapping rules determine business field correspondence.
output: The purchasing integration validates the translated JSON before creating an idempotent order in the ERP system.
check: Reconcile partner identifiers, line-item quantities and rejected transactions using representative EDI samples.

title: measure campaign overlap without exchanging raw customer tables
input: Two partners prepare permitted customer datasets and agree on the allowed overlap analysis.
action: Clean Rooms applies configured-table analysis rules to collaboration queries. Participants control permitted columns and query constraints; the collaboration does not freely disclose each partner's raw customer table.
output: The authorized result recipient receives the permitted aggregate overlap result for campaign planning.
check: Try an allowed aggregate and a disallowed identifying query; inspect output-size restrictions before sharing results.

title: replace a historical CodeStar project with explicit delivery resources
input: The maintainer inventories a historical project's repository, build, deployment and team permissions.
action: CodeStar historically assembled a project toolchain and project dashboard. Existing underlying repository, build and deployment resources must be managed individually when replacing that project coordination layer.
output: The release owner reconstructs the pipeline with explicit CodeBuild and deployment configuration and reviewed access roles.
check: Build and deploy the retained revision without relying on the retired project dashboard or project membership shortcuts.

title: inspect an incident from a managed mobile device
input: The on-call engineer signs in to the intended account with the permitted mobile console identity.
action: The mobile application displays supported AWS resources and operational information and permits supported actions under the signed-in identity. It provides a mobile management interface, not an application runtime.
output: The engineer checks the affected resource and performs only the supported, approved incident action.
check: Confirm the account and Region, verify the action in the service and preserve the incident record.

title: upload a large prepared dataset through a transfer terminal
input: The dataset owner prepares encrypted media, upload credentials and the reserved terminal visit.
action: Data Transfer Terminal provides a physical location and high-bandwidth connectivity for customer equipment to transfer data to AWS. Customer software performs the authorized upload to the chosen storage destination.
output: The ingest team uses the transferred S3 objects after access and integrity checks.
check: Reconcile object sizes and checksums, then revoke transfer credentials and retain the original until acceptance.

title: render a film sequence on a managed worker fleet
input: The artist submits scene assets, frame ranges and renderer dependencies to the studio queue.
action: Deadline Cloud schedules submitted render jobs onto compatible workers in the configured farm and queue. Workers run the selected renderer with the approved job attachments and software licensing configuration.
output: The studio retrieves completed frames from the configured output storage and assembles the reviewed sequence.
check: Check frame coverage, failed-task retries, attachment access and rendering output before final delivery.
